page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and does not bundle local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling due to the dual-vCPU configuration. Single-core tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the average tier. Single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 also demonstrate average performance. However, multi-core benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, fall into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also register in the bottom 10%, reflecting the resource constraints of this smaller instance size.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g7.large offers a balanced resource profile for entry-level workloads without the overhead of local storage or high-end accelerators. Given its moderate single-core performance and lower multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics, this instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose applications. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, small-scale development or testing environments, simple text processing, and low-throughput background tasks that do not require intensive parallel processing or high memory throughput.
